evidence_graph.quote: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing ∗

We use deep neural networks to estimate an asset pricing model for individual stock returns that takes advantage of the vast amount of conditioning information, while keeping a fully ﬂexible form and accounting for time-variation.
Our goal is to explain the diﬀerences in the cross-section of returns R for individual stocks.

Our optimal model has two layers, four economic states and eight instruments for the test assets.
The optimal model is evaluated on the test data.

base_method_card.title: Deep Learning in Asset Pricing ∗
base_method_card.task_type: conditional asset pricing / stochastic discount factor estimation
base_method_card.label_definition: Next-month individual stock excess return, defined as stock return minus the one-month Treasury bill risk-free rate.
data_requirements: Monthly equity return data for all securities on CRSP from January 1967 to December 2016.
One-month Treasury bill rates from the Kenneth French Data Library to compute excess returns.
Macroeconomic time series used to extract time-varying economic states.
base_method_card.training_protocol: Train the SDF model on 1967-1986 data, tune hyperparameters on 1987-1991 validation data by maximizing the validation Sharpe ratio of the SDF, and evaluate the selected model on 1992-2016 test data. Neural-network models are ensembled by averaging outputs from nine fits with the same architecture and different optimization starting values. The optimal reported GAN configuration has two layers, four economic states, and eight conditioning instruments for the test assets. Optimizer, epochs, batch size, random seeds, and early-stopping rule are unknown from the supplied context.
base_method_card.evaluation_protocol: Fixed chronological split: training sample 1967-1986, validation sample 1987-1991, out-of-sample testing sample 1992-2016. The optimal model selected on validation data is evaluated once on the test data. Metrics are computed for the SDF factor and individual stock residuals: unconditional Sharpe ratio, explained variation, and cross-sectional R2.
strict_requirements: Use monthly CRSP equity return data covering January 1967 through December 2016.

Select hyperparameters by maximizing the SDF Sharpe ratio on the validation data.
Use the optimal GAN model configuration with two layers, four economic states, and eight instruments for the test assets.
Average neural-network outputs across nine model fits for the ensemble.
Evaluate using SDF Sharpe ratio, explained variation, and XS-R2 on the test sample.
